chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Clyde Bernhardt's Saydisk record he did not realize was commercial
summary: Clyde invited him to record and he didn't know it was commercial until handed an envelope of pay.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: But before that, you did some recordings that I managed to get you out for.
For Clyde and Derek Stuart Baxter you did one.
That's Clyde's contact and Clyde's record date.

Yeah. Well, see, I didn't know that was going to be a commercial record. Clyde asked me would I like to make some records with him. You know, why not? But I thought he was just getting it for his own amusement, doing it for his own amusement, for himself, you know. So I told him, sure, I'd make some records with him. I thought maybe he was making some demos or something.

So when I get to the studio and we get through with the recordings, then they hand me an envelope. I said, 'What is this?' 'That's what you get for making the recbrds.' I said, 'Well, I wasn't expecting to be paid for this.' I didn't know this was a commercial gig.' He said, 'Well, now ...(?)...(?)...' That's how he got, you know, the record (?). I thought that was just something he wanted some
records for his own amusement or something. I didn't know he was going to commercialize it. Yeah, I should have put my date(?) in and had my name on it.
